novelty_basis: Searches (2026-10-18): 'symmetric difference' + Seidel spectrum; Kronecker product of Seidel matrices / two-graphs; tensor product of two-graphs. Only the special case with an edgeless factor, S(D_m(G)) + I = J_m (x) (S(G) + I), was found (a paper on Seidel equienergetic graphs, seen through a secondary summary). The symmetric-difference product itself is Harary-Wilcox (1967). One-line observation; plausibly known to two-graph specialists.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C14.md Theorem 6); entry-level identity in Lean (xor_character); exact integer check for all pairs of graphs with <= 3 vertices (EXP-C14-06); spectra on 30 random pairs (EXP-C14-03)
statement:
For all graphs G, H: S(G xor H) + I = (S(G) + I) (x) (S(H) + I), where xor is the symmetric-difference product
and S the Seidel matrix. Hence the Seidel eigenvalues of G xor H are (theta+1)(eta+1) - 1, and xor is
compatible with Seidel switching, giving a commutative associative product on two-graphs with unit [K1].
title: The symmetric-difference product is the Kronecker product of Seidel matrices; it acts on two-graphs
